title: The box model and spacing
lesson:
Every element is a **box**, from the inside out:
1. **content** (the text or image),
2. **padding** (space inside the border),
3. **border**,
4. **margin** (space outside, pushing other boxes away).

`padding: 12px` sets all four sides; `padding: 8px 16px` is top/bottom then left/right; `margin: 0 auto` centres a block that has a width.

By default, `width` means the content only, so padding and border make a box *wider* than you said. Almost every site fixes that with one rule at the top:

```
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
```

Now `width: 100%` really is 100%, padding included. Use it.

`max-width` keeps text from stretching across a wide screen (lines longer than about 75 characters are hard to read): `main { max-width: 760px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 16px; }` is a good page frame. Elements are either **block** (take the full width, start on a new line: div, p, h1) or **inline** (sit in the line of text: a, b, span).
